conventions.draws: `draws` lists each party's random values in the order it takes them. A `bytes` draw fills a request of exactly that length; a `u32` draw answers a request for a 32-bit integer. Host: invitation id (16), ticket secret (16), for send link the first code (u32, drawn again while at least 4294000000); then for each new attempt, after the debit and before reading its first message, the next code (u32, only while attempts are left) and the CPace scalar yb (32). Joiner: for each attempt the attempt id (16) and the CPace scalar ya (32).
conventions.exporters: On connection n both ends see the join exporter n repeated 32 times and the pair exporter n + 100 repeated 32 times.
conventions.joiners: Each joiner's identity secret is one byte repeated 32 times: 0x50 for the first joiner a sequence names, 0x51 for the second, and so on. Its name is its letter.

description: Attempt-limit and resend sequences for the send-link flow (spec wire.md, "Send-link flow and the code" and "Attempt limits"), plus one-enrollment for in person. Each step runs one operation and then the listed expectations hold. Ops: connect (the connection starts; after the two HELLO messages the joiner sends its join proof on conn and the host's AUTHORIZED, if any, reaches the joiner), submit (the joiner enters a code; messages flow until both sides stop), submit_first (only the joiner's first message reaches the host; the host's reply is recorded in `out` but not delivered to the joiner), redeliver (that first message reaches the host again on conn; the reply is recorded, not delivered), inject (the joiner's side sends `message` for `attempt`, "current" meaning the attempt of its last submit, with `payload`; the reply is recorded, not delivered), drop (conn closes), approve (host owner taps for conn). Codes: right (the code the host shows now), wrong (000000, or 000001 if 000000 is shown), stale (the code the host showed when the previous attempt started). `reply`: first_reply (the same messages, byte for byte, as the host's answer to that first message), code_abort (the host's only answer is CODE_ABORT pairing_failed for that attempt), none (no answer). `new_code` says whether the host showed a fresh code during the step. `closed` lists connections the host closed during the step. When `joiner_state` becomes failed with a code, the joiner also closes the connection with GOAWAY of that code after its listed messages, unless the host had already closed it (wire.md 10.6 rule 9); that close is not listed. `out` lists, in order, every control message each side sent during the step (`send`), host closes (`close`) and codes the host showed (`show_code`), except the HELLO each side sends first on every connection (wire.md, "Connection start and step 2"): a replay over real connections exchanges both HELLOs, checks the agreed version and starts comparing at JOIN_PROOF. Each side's sends keep their own order; on connect the two sides send independently, and `out` lists the joiner's before the host's.

sequences.description: The host answered msg_a; then the joiner aborts the attempt. The abort ends the attempt and keeps its debit, but changes neither kept value: msg_a again gets the same msg_b, byte for byte. A different payload on the ended attempt gets code_abort, with no debit. An abort for an attempt the host does not have is ignored.
sequences.name: resend_after_the_joiner_aborted

sequences.description: After msg_a, a different payload on the running attempt is read as msg_c: 64 zero bytes are a wrong confirmation, so the attempt fails with code_abort. The kept payload is now those 64 bytes, so msg_a again is a different payload on an ended attempt: code_abort, with no debit.
sequences.name: different_payload_on_a_running_attempt_is_the_next_message

sequences.description: First messages of two new attempts that fail before any group work: a share that is the identity point, then a share with a wrong length byte. Each is debited and the host draws the next code and the CPace scalar before reading it, then answers code_abort. The right code then pairs. The draws list shows the order.
sequences.name: bad_first_message_still_uses_the_draws

sequences.description: Joiner a's first message is replayed on b's connection. The attempt id was already seen on another connection, so the host refuses it with code_abort before any debit or exchange work, and shows no new code.
sequences.name: attempt_replayed_on_another_connection_is_refused
